dataset.name: MarineCadastre / NOAA AIS vessel traffic, broadcast-point CSV, 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-02
dataset.product: daily CSV (compressed .csv.zst present locally); not the GeoParquet product
dataset.retrieval_date: unknown (local file mtime of .zst: 2026-10-18; organizer-provided subsets)
dataset.subset_rules: Organizer subsets are byte-identical head-prefixes of ais-2026-01-01.csv (verified with cmp); never combined with each other. jan01_02 = the Jan 1 and Jan 2 daily files ingested together (day-partitioned). Region filter: all; deterministic vessel sample of 4000 MMSIs by hash key.
dataset.missing_value_policy: SOG>=102.2 (102.3 sentinel) -> null; COG>=360 -> null; heading>=360 (511) -> null; lat/lon out of range or (0,0) dropped; duplicate (mmsi,timestamp) -> first kept. These are OBSERVED source problems, handled before any injected defects.
dataset.rights_statement: NOAA/BOEM MarineCadastre data are U.S. Government public data; check the product metadata/terms before redistribution. Raw data are not redistributed in this repo (data/ is git-ignored).

task.evaluation_proxy: first later AIS report of the same MMSI within horizon +/- tolerance; a noisy proxy, not verified truth

split.rule: vessel-disjoint (hash(mmsi)%10<3 -> test) AND chronological: train targets end before split_t; test decisions start at split_t + horizon and need >=45 min of vessel history
split.holdout: window 4 (latest period) plus the 'holdout_unseen_bias' defect type not used when designing the countermeasure

model.retraining: trained once on nominal data; NOT retrained during the degradation progression

defect_configuration.progression: SIMULATED degradation progression over 5 real chronological test windows
defect_configuration.lowq_defects: jitter N(0,200 m) on state and previous fix; 25% gross outlier 3-15 km; SOG scaled x0.3-2.5 (25%), missing (15%), raw 102.3 sentinel (10%); COG random (30%), missing (15%), else +N(0,5 deg); heading dropped
defect_configuration.holdout_unseen_bias: constant 1.5 km offset at bearing 60 deg on the delivered fix
defect_configuration.synthetic_msgs_simulated: reliable_msgs * share/(1-share); a simulated volume, not measured

modification_log: Raw CSVs unchanged. Ingest writes cache/parquet (raw values). Cleaning and all injected defects occur in memory; injected defects are labelled per case (columns source, defects, is_stale, is_lowq) and kept separate from observed source problems.

countermeasure.defer_penalty_rule: p90 of nominal unmitigated error, charged per deferred case in policy_cost_km so that abstaining on everything cannot win

data_quality.definition: interpretable per-record flag codes (aisdp/quality.py FLAG_CODES), raw records unchanged; flag counts in quality_flags.csv, per-vessel codes in quality_vessels.parquet
data_quality.limits: file row order is not preserved by the source/ingest, so out-of-order timestamps cannot be detected; AIS reception time and message source IDs are not in the data

reporting_gaps.definition: observation/reporting gap = consecutive reports of one MMSI further apart than max(600s, 5.0 x the vessel's median cadence); NOT a proven radio failure (coverage, product downsampling and leaving the area look identical). possible_coverage_exit = gap starts/ends in a sparse reception cell.
reporting_gaps.synthetic_test: real clean tracks with one run of records withheld (never delivered) or delayed (delivered 20 min late); labels known; see gap_synthetic_test.csv

traffic_density.question: How busy will this area be?
traffic_density.target: unique MMSIs (valid vessel MID 201-775) with >=1 report in a 0.25 deg grid cell during the next 60 min [o, o+60min); per-area rate = count / spherical cell area
traffic_density.unit_index: cells with >=1 vessel report in the training period; a cell without reports in a covered bucket is a confirmed zero; origins whose lookback/target touches a bucket with no source data at all are excluded
traffic_density.model: HistGradientBoostingRegressor (absolute_error) on the change from persistence; baselines: persistence, 3-hour rolling mean, training-period cell mean
traffic_density.split: chronological: origins whose target window ends before split_t train; origins >= split_t test (same cells in both: an area forecast, not a cell-disjoint split); overlapping 60-min windows at a 15-min stride are correlated, so case counts overstate independent evidence

port_occupancy.question: How congested will this port be? (answered only as an AIS occupancy PROXY)
port_occupancy.target: unique MMSIs with >=1 report at SOG < 1 kn inside a port/anchorage study zone in the next 60 min
port_occupancy.zones: study zones = 0.1 deg cells where >= 10 distinct vessels had a >=30-min dwell ending before split_t (top 60); NOT verified port/berth boundaries, no names
port_occupancy.not_measured: berth capacity, queue length, waiting time, terminal throughput; the count is an underestimate when reports are missing

destination.question: Where is this vessel going?
destination.label: first dwell (>=30 min with max SOG < 1 kn per 10-min bucket) starting after the decision and within 6 h, mapped to an inferred arrival zone (0.05 deg cell with >= 3 distinct vessels dwelling in the training period). Training labels use only data before split_t. Statuses: arrival_zone | arrival_unzoned | no_arrival_in_window | censored; only arrival_zone cases are scored (accuracy is conditional on an observed zoned arrival).
destination.model: candidate-zone ranker: HistGradientBoostingClassifier on (decision, zone) pairs within reach; abstains when no zone is in reach (and, in the quality-aware pipeline, on low top score or failed input checks). Scores are normalised model scores, not calibrated probabilities.
destination.baseline: heading-aligned nearest zone (|bearing - COG| <= 30 deg first, then distance)
destination.split: vessel-disjoint (same MMSI hash as the position task) and chronological (train decisions before split_t, test decisions after it with >= 45 min of history)
destination.not_claimed: named ports, verified berth calls, cargo delivery, declared AIS destination

tasks.stress_tests: same SIMULATED feed-degradation design as the position task: nominal / stale / low quality / combined x mitigation off/on, on identical test cases and unmodified targets, frozen models, seeds as configured. Counts: stale = latest 15-60 min of buckets not yet delivered; low quality = SYN-FASTFEED ghost IDs (invalid, transient, persistent), tripled messages, omissions. Destination: the position task's stale states and SYN-FASTFEED record defects.
